attributes.body_ja:
「ところが」は、名詞（めいし）の「ところ」と接続助詞（せつぞくじょし）の「が」からできた接続詞（せつぞくし）です。「(A) になると思（おも）っていたのに、実際（じっさい）には (B) になった」ことを表（あらわ）します。

「ところが」は、たいてい、前（まえ）の文（ぶん）で述（の）べられたことと反対（はんたい）のことを述（の）べる時（とき）に、文（ぶん）の頭（あたま）で使（つか）われます。

このような使（つか）い方（かた）の「が」は、「確定（かくてい）の逆接（ぎゃくせつ）」と呼（よ）ばれます。これは、何（なに）かが起（お）こったあとで、それとは反対（はんたい）の結果（けっか）や出来事（できごと）が続（つづ）くことを表（あらわ）します。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「ところが」は、思（おも）っていたこととは違（ちが）う出来事（できごと）が起（お）こることを表（あらわ）すので、話（はな）し手（て）の意思（いし）では変（か）えられなことに使（つか）われます。ただし、「失敗（しっぱい）すると思（おも）っていたけど、うまくいった」ときのように、良（よ）い意味（いみ）で意外（いがい）だったことにも使（つか）うことができます。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「ところが」は、一（ひと）つの接続詞（せつぞくし）とされることもあります。話題（わだい）を変（か）えるときに使（つか）う「ところで」も、同（おな）じように一（ひと）つの語（ご）とされる接続助詞（せつぞくじょし）です。
attributes.body:
ところが is a conjunction in Japanese that is a combination of the noun, ところ 'place', and the conjunction particle が. It is used to highlight that (A) was expected, but the unexpected result (B) occurred. It is usually translated as 'however', or 'despite that'.

ところが is most often used at the beginning of a new sentence, before highlighting something that is contrary to what was described in the previous sentence.

This use of が in Japanese is referred to as 確定（かくてい）の逆接（ぎゃくせつ）, which basically means 'a contradictory conclusion'.

Caution

Because ところが highlights a result that is unexpected, it can only be used for things that are beyond the control of the speaker. However, if the speaker is trying to do something, but assumes that their attempt may result in failure, ところが can be used to show that they were unexpectedly successful.

Fun Fact

Sometimes, ところが is referred to as a conjunction particle itself, disregarding the combination of ところ and が. This is similar to ところで, another conjunction particle that has a slightly different meaning, and is frequently translated as 'by the way'.

attributes.description: それでも vs. ところが

attributes.body: Both express contrast, but with different nuance. ところが introduces an unexpected result, e.g. 試合に勝つと思った。ところが負けた ('I thought we'd win the game. But we lost.') それにしても acknowledges the situation but adds an emotional reaction or further judgment, e.g. 仕方がない。それにしても悔しい ('It can't be helped. Even so, it's frustrating.')

first_relatable.title: ところが
first_relatable.meaning: Even so, However, Even though, But

attributes.body: Both introduce unexpected outcomes, but differ in type of surprise. 却って means the result was the opposite of what was intended or expected, e.g. 謝ったら却って怒られた ('When I apologized, I was yelled at instead.') ところが highlights a surprising turn of events, though not necessarily the exact opposite, e.g. 田中さんに電話をかけた。ところがもう出発していた ('I called Tanaka. But he had already departed.')

attributes.body: Both だが・ですが and ところが express contrast, but with different nuances. だが・ですが is a neutral transition similar to 'but' or 'however,' and can appear in various positions within a sentence. ところが usually comes at the start of a sentence and emphasizes an unexpected or surprising result, often appearing in storytelling or narration.

second_relatable.title: ところが
second_relatable.meaning: Even so, However, Even though, But

attributes.body: Both ところが and が express contrast or contradiction. ところが is used at the beginning of a sentence to emphasize a contrast between expectation and reality. In contrast, が is used after a phrase or at the end of a sentence to express simple contrast, or sometimes to add information or context without implying surprise or expectation.

second_relatable.title: ところが
second_relatable.meaning: Even so, However, Even though, But

attributes.body: Both ところが and けど・だけど express contrast or contradiction. The key difference is that ところが is used at the beginning of a sentence to emphasize a contrast between the expected result and reality, and is more formal. In contrast, けど・だけど are used after a phrase or at the end of a sentence to express simple contrast or contradiction.

first_relatable.title: ところが
first_relatable.meaning: Even so, However, Even though, But

attributes.body: それでも and ところが both show contrast, like 'even so' or 'and yet'. それでも has a neutral tone and simply adds something that goes against the previous statement. ところが implies something unexpected or surprising happened, especially outside the speaker's control.

first_relatable.meaning: But still, And yet, Even so, Nevertheless

second_relatable.title: ところが
second_relatable.meaning: Even so, However, Even though, But

attributes.body: Both ところが and けれども are linking phrases used to express contrast. けれども (or the casual form けど) shows a simple contrast or transition, similar to 'but' in English, and can appear mid-sentence or at the end. In contrast, ところが is typically used at the beginning of a sentence and adds a strong nuance of surprise or something unexpected.
